title: sequential-cohort-escrow-rollout-with-resumable-failover-and-telemetry-hooks
author: Aisha Kramer
description:
Problem: Current cohort rollouts occasionally leave a small fraction of users in an inconsistent state when an immediate rollback is triggered mid-phased-swap (observed in incidents SUP-4021 and ENG-1284). Root cause analysis showed race between drain fences and the traffic allocator, and lack of a resumable state for partially-evicted cohorts.

Goal: Introduce a sequential cohort escrow lane that provides: 1) deterministic eviction and resume semantics for cohort slices, 2) a small safety escrow budget that can be consumed to allow fast rollback without user-visible failure, and 3) telemetry hooks that annotate rollout timeline events to make post-mortem for partial rollbacks trivial.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a new rollout orchestration mode "sequential-cohort-escrow" that runs cohort slices one at a time in an escrowed lane. Each cohort slice commits when both health probes and telemetry anchor events pass. On failure, the controller can perform a resumable failover which drains cohorts deterministically and optionally consumes escrow capacity (configurable per-Linear ticket). The implementation is integrated with the router (servegraph) and the Console observability pipeline to emit annotations for tracing/alerts.

Key features implemented in this change: - CohortEscrow controller: state machine with states {Pending, Escrowed, Active, Draining, Evicted, ResumableFailover}. The controller persists minimal markers to rolloutmetadata so retries are idempotent. - Safety escrow budget: new per-rollout quota that is charged only when an accelerated rollback path is used; surfaced in Console and APIs. - Deterministic drain sequences: router changes traffic in a two-phase commit to avoid split-brain session affinity for session-affine cohorts. - Telemetry hooks and annotations: rollout events (escrow-granted, escrow-consumed, cohort-commit, cohort-evict, resumable-failover-start/end) are emitted as structured tags to tracing and metrics backends. - Resumable failover API: endpoint to resume a previously failed rollout after manual verification (or automated after alerts cleared).

Why this is different from other rollout modes: Existing progressive and canary controllers assume ephemeral, all-or-nothing commits. This PR introduces explicitly escrowed lanes and resume semantics for partial commits to support long-lived user sessions and regulated workflows where immediate global rollback is dangerous.

Compatibility and defaults: This mode is opt-in and off by default. Existing rollouts are unaffected unless admins select the "sequential-cohort-escrow" strategy. Backwards compatibility is ensured via compatibility shim in the scheduler that translates old rollout configs transparently.

Related work and references: Linear ENG-1284 and ENG-1285 track the design and follow-ups. Support ticket SUP-4021 provided incident traces used in testing. Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1284/sequential-cohort-escrow-design (internal).

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by SRE/product - [x] Unit + integration tests added for controller state transitions - [x] End-to-end test in perf-canary sandbox (small traffic partition) - [x] Console surface and docs stubbed - [x] Feature gated and disabled by default

4b5c6de: router: two-phase commit traffic drain primitives and session-affine hints
7e8f901: api: expose resumable-failover endpoint and safety-escrow configuration
ab12cd3: observability: emit rollout telemetry hooks and structured span tags

review_conversation: Diego Martins (reviewer): Left a note about potential race in drain_coordinator when a second eviction overlaps; requested explicit lock ordering.
Author (Aisha Kramer): Addressed by introducing coordinator.LockOrder() and added unit tests to assert no double-evict behavior.
Samir Patel (reviewer): Asked for clearer eviction telemetry to include cohort-id and request-sample for debugging.
Author: Added cohort-id tag and sampled request example to telemetry_emit.go; included an anonymized sample in the E2E test.
Lina Zhou (approver): Verified integration with Console and asked to gate safety-escrow toggles behind admin feature flag; requested docs for operators.
Author: Added admin gate and operator docs; included migration notes and recommended budget defaults.
ci_checks: perf-benchmark: perf-canary run (baseline +5% tail latency on 99th token under escrow mode; within SLA)
notes_on_testing: Ran the escrow flow in perf-canary with synthetic session-affine traffic; validated resumable flow by injecting failure at commit; validated telemetry anchors in Console and traces. Recorded the incident replay artifacts in SUP-4021 for auditors.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in rollout strategy 'sequential-cohort-escrow' that provides deterministic cohort commit and resumable failover with safety escrow budgeting. Admins must opt-in and configure the escrow budget; see docs/rollouts/strategies/sequential-escrow.md for details.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-02-18 by Diego Martins. Merge commit summarizes controller, router, api, observability and docs changes. Post-merge: feature gated off by default; rollout to internal canary set for 2026-02-25.
post_merge_actions: Create rollout tutorial in docs site outlining operator steps
Add Console dashboard tiles for escrow usage and consumed budget
Schedule follow-up work to add automated remediation when escrow budget approaches threshold (ENG-1285)
